Ok, so I was reading his [Wikipedia entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Meyer) earlier:

> Meyer is a devout Roman Catholic and on several occasions has referred to the head coaching position at the University of Notre Dame as his "dream job," leading to speculation that he would someday wish to coach there. However, according to a July 2009 newspaper report, Meyer insisted he would never leave Florida for Notre Dame. And when the employment status of Irish coach Charlie Weis came into question in November 2009, Meyer held a press conference to dispel rumors linking him to the possible opening, stating that he would remain at Florida for "as long as they'll have me."

Well, we all know what happened. Saban beat him in the SEC Championship and he went to the hospital a day later. He announced his resignation later that month, and although he stuck around for a year, he had one foot out the door, left after the 2010 season, and didn't even coach in 2011. He formally accepted the tOSU job in Nov 2011.

Now, this was a convenient time to leave the SEC, and I'm sure he was pinging major programs in the Big10, Big12, ACC, PAC10, etc. throughout 2009-11 to see where he might be able to resurrect another major program. After all, he sure timed his SEC entry well - 2005, right as USC's dominance was ending. Meyer is the king of [power vacuums](http://www.industrialairsolutions.com/images/Power-Vac-Gas.jpg).

It appears he's done the same with the B1G. He went undefeated his first year, 12-2 his second, won a national championship in his third, and probably could've repeated last year. Michigan's new impetus to chase OSU has made them relevant again. Iowa came out of nowhere. Wisconsin is usually bowl caliber, and Michigan State made the playoffs. Northwestern was no pushover last year, and expect Penn State and/or Maryland to play some hard ball soon. The B1G is about to be the best conference in college football.

Eventually, Urban might feel the heat again and jump ship for another program. He only spent 2 years at Utah, 5 years at Florida (6 counting 2010), and he's going on Year 5 now at tOSU. How many more years will Brian Kelly be in South Bend, where he's averaging almost 4 losses a year? All the historic power programs have won a championship recently (Oklahoma in 2000, Ohio State in 2001 and 2014, USC in 2004, Texas in 2005, Alabama 4 times since 2009), how much longer will Notre Dame wait?

I think Urban Meyer will bail on tOSU and retire at Notre Dame. He's only 51. But what if he'd already gone there in 2010?

Brian Kelly *got* to the 2012 championship game with most of his own players. But if Meyer had taken that job in 2010, he likely would've *won* a national championship in his 2nd or 3rd year, based purely on his performance at Florida and Ohio State.

So, not only would Urban Meyer have his third national championship (like the won with Ohio State), but possibly another. Nick Saban is up to about a national championship every two years since taking over at Alabama in 2007. Urban Meyer isn't far behind, with about one every four years since taking over Florida in 2005. However, if he'd taken the Notre Dame job in 2010, Urban Meyer would probably have two championships in South Bend, meaning his count would be up to four. Let's assume he beat Saban in 2012, and that drops Saban to three. Of course, if Meyer weren't coaching OSU in 2014, Saban might have won the inaugural playoffs, meaning they'd be tied at four apiece.

But Notre Dame plays a harder schedule, or at least a more challenging one than B1G teams were playing when Urban arrived for the 2012 season, so who knows what would've happened.
